newsitem.title: UK: Analyst sees Cuba sugar crop steady, depends on US.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees Cuba sugar crop steady, depends on US.

text.p: Cuba's annual sugar output should stabilise at up to 5.0 million tonnes provided the U.S. continues to waive a provision of the controversial Helms-Burton law, an F.O. Licht analyst said on Thursday.

"If we see a continued waiving of Title III of the law, there are some chances that Cuban sugar production will stablilise at around 4.5 and 5.0 million tonnes," Christoph Berg told a conference hosted by Agra Europe.

He was referring to a provision of the law -- the latest revision to the long-standing U.S. trade embargo against the communist-ruled island -- which was again waived by President Clinton in January for six months.

The provision would allow U.S. citizens, including Cubans who left after the 1959 revolution and now naturalised U.S. citizens, to sue foreign companies deemed to be benefiting from their property seized by the communist government.
"The longer-term perspectives depend on various factors -- the U.S. stance on Helms-Burton and the ways in which European allies are able to dilute some aspects of this law," Berg said.
He added that 1996/97 would be a "very difficult year" for Cuba's sugar industry.
